paper.title_en: X-ray polarimetry of a magnetar in the aftermath of an anti-glitch: Revisiting 1E 2259+586 with IXPE
paper.abstract_en: Magnetars display timing anomalies such as glitches and anti-glitches. 1E 2259+586, whose properties in the X-ray band were recently investigated through a joint XMM/IXPE observation campaign, has been observed to have multiple glitches and three anti-glitches, the most recent occurring in May 2025. Although the X-ray emission is currently decaying, the flux, which roughly doubled at the onset of the anti-glitch, had not yet returned to its original level at the time of the IXPE observation, and the pulse profile has also shown significant evolution. We present an analysis of the recent IXPE observation of 1E 2259+586 from late April to early May 2026. We compare the post-anti-glitch polarisation results with those obtained from the previous IXPE observation in 2023. This provides an unprecedented opportunity to monitor the spectro-polarimetric evolution of a magnetar in the wake of a hallmark event such as an anti-glitch. A dedicated 400ks IXPE DDT observation was approved to track possible changes in the polarisation with respect to the pre-anti-glitch campaign. Spectral and polarimetric properties were jointly modelled within the xspec and ixpeobssim suites, and the analysis was further expanded using a maximum-likelihood technique. No significant detection was found in the phase-averaged and energy-integrated spectrum of this observation. However, despite the significantly shorter exposure, polarisation was clearly detected in the phase-resolved spectrum and the degree of polarisation was found to have a higher best-fitting value, though still statistically consistent, than the previous measurement from 2023, reaching a level >30% in correspondence to the pulse profile minimum. In spite of some slight differences between the two observations, the polarisation trends remain largely consistent and indicate that the source has mostly returned to its pre-event state.
